01-context.mmd: Shows the four user situations, functional modules, account/data services and the mobile distribution boundary.
Makes product responsibilities explicit without confusing TestFlight with a runtime workout service.
02-architecture.mmd: Separates device UI/controllers, local repositories/SQLite/outbox and hosted Supabase Auth/API/PostgreSQL. EAS and TestFlight are a separate build path.
Explains why confirming a set is local and why the API still needs owner checks, idempotency and atomic writes.
03-navigation.mmd: Maps launch, authentication, resume, main areas, typed entry, summary, history drill-down, templates and sync review.
Gives both coding models the same reachable screen flows; no story should exist only as an isolated service method.
04-data-model.mmd: Models workout/entry/set records, stable exercises, independent template lists, settings and local/server synchronization records.
Prevents list templates from accidentally copying sets, preserves entered units, and makes deletion/deduplication data explicit.
classes/01-ui-and-auth.mmd: Class model: controllers and account access
Defines each feature controller, auth gateway/session storage and bootstrap responsibilities. Routes/components delegate to these logical controllers.
Connects user actions to domain operations while keeping Supabase details out of screen code.
classes/02-domain.mmd: Class model: domain entities and services
Defines typed workout records, exercise/template/settings entities, validation, service operations and enum values.
Makes exercise-type rules, active/finished states, stable identity and template independence implementable rather than implicit.
classes/03-persistence-and-sync.mmd: Class model: repositories and backend handlers
Defines repository ports, SQLite adapters, transactions, sync coordination/gateway and logical PostgreSQL handlers.
Supplies the database-handler and API-controller responsibilities required by the assignment and supports failure recovery.
classes/04-presentation.mmd: Class model: conversion, progress and readability
Defines shared unit conversion, volume/reps aggregation, periods/points, summaries, chart tables and text-scale presentation.
Ensures graphs and plain summaries use the same numbers, and display conversion never corrupts originals.
classes/05-sync-records.mmd: Details operation snapshots, preserved conflicts, checkpoints, remote receipts and ordered change events.
Makes duplicate prevention, resumable pull and conflict preservation concrete types with durable fields.
sequence/SUP-01-auth-and-bootstrap.mmd: Shows first online sign-in, offline reopening of a known account, owner-partition initialization and sign-out safeguards.
Fills the selected specification's sign-in assumption without silently mixing account data or dropping pending work.
sequence/SUP-02-conflict-resolution.mmd: Shows presentation of preserved local/remote versions and explicit, validated resolution.
Resolves the source's undefined two-device-offline rule without a silent last-write-wins overwrite.
sequence/FW-01.mmd: FW-01: Start a workout, add exercises
As Marcus, I want to start a workout and add exercises as I go, so that I can log in the order I actually train. The flow identifies its UI controller, domain service and data boundary.
Specifies active-workout uniqueness and ordered exercise entry before logging.
sequence/FW-02.mmd: FW-02: Record a set with prefill

As Marcus, I want to record a set by entering weight and reps, prefilled from my previous set, so that I can log between sets without losing rest time. The flow identifies its UI controller, domain service and data boundary.
Makes prefill precedence and durable confirmation explicit for the central recording interaction.
sequence/FW-03.mmd: FW-03: Set form matches exercise type

As Elena, I want the set form to ask only for what applies to the exercise, so that I am not forced to enter a weight for push-ups or planks. The flow identifies its UI controller, domain service and data boundary.
Prevents irrelevant weight/repetition fields from leaking into other exercise types.
sequence/FW-04.mmd: As Priya, I want to see what I did the last time I performed an exercise while I log it, so that I can choose today’s weight instead of guessing. The flow identifies its UI controller, domain service and data boundary.
Defines which prior session is shown and how local corrections affect it.
sequence/FW-05.mmd: FW-05: Correct or remove a set or entry

As Marcus, I want to correct or remove a set, or remove an entry, during a workout, so that one mistaken tap does not corrupt my history. The flow identifies its UI controller, domain service and data boundary.
Preserves correction, confirmation and immediate undo behavior without renumbering corruption.
sequence/FW-06.mmd: As Tomás, I want to finish a workout and see a short, plain summary, so that I know it is saved and can read what I did. The flow identifies its UI controller, domain service and data boundary.
Distinguishes a locally saved finish from a successfully uploaded record.
sequence/FW-07.mmd: As Priya, I want my unfinished workout to still be there if I switch apps or my phone locks, so that an interruption does not cost me the session. The flow identifies its UI controller, domain service and data boundary.
Requires actual process-restart persistence rather than an in-memory resume flag.
sequence/FW-08.mmd: FW-08: Record a workout on an earlier date

As Elena, I want to record a workout I already did by choosing an earlier date, so that I can catch up when I could not use my phone during the session. The flow identifies its UI controller, domain service and data boundary.
Separates a training calendar date from timestamps so delayed logging is graphed correctly.
sequence/FW-09.mmd: As Elena, I want to log a workout when I have no connection and have it uploaded later, so that I never lose a session because of my signal. The flow identifies its UI controller, domain service and data boundary.
Models the highest-risk cross-system path, including retries, receipts, conflicts and pull checkpoints.
sequence/FW-10.mmd: As Priya, I want to choose whether weights are shown in kg or lb, so that entries match the plates and machines I use. The flow identifies its UI controller, domain service and data boundary.
Keeps account display preferences separate from immutable entered measurements.
sequence/FW-11.mmd: FW-11: Find an exercise; recent first

As Priya, I want to find an exercise by typing part of its name or filtering by muscle group, with recent ones first, so that I can add the right exercise without knowing its exact name. The flow identifies its UI controller, domain service and data boundary.
Makes combined search/filter and offline recent ordering consistent for both implementations.
sequence/FW-12.mmd: As Elena, I want to create my own exercise with a name and a type, so that I can log home and unusual movements the library lacks. The flow identifies its UI controller, domain service and data boundary.
Specifies private custom exercise creation, name conflicts and eventual type locking.
sequence/FW-13.mmd: FW-13: Rename or archive a custom exercise
As Marcus, I want to rename or archive a custom exercise, so that I can tidy my library without losing history. The flow identifies its UI controller, domain service and data boundary.
Keeps rename/archive changes attached to stable exercise identities and historical sets.
sequence/FW-14.mmd: As Tomás, I want to see a list of my finished workouts with dates, exercises and number of sets, so that I can quickly check when and what I trained. The flow identifies its UI controller, domain service and data boundary.
Defines an accessible paged list with stable ordering and an honest empty state.
sequence/FW-15.mmd: As Marcus, I want to open a past workout and see every exercise and set as recorded, so that I can plan a repeat or check what I did. The flow identifies its UI controller, domain service and data boundary.
Provides complete, current records without forcing users through graphs.
sequence/FW-16.mmd: As Marcus, I want to see every time I performed one exercise, with the sets from each session, so that I can follow one lift in numbers. The flow identifies its UI controller, domain service and data boundary.
Makes exercise-level history reachable and robust to renaming/archiving.
sequence/FW-17.mmd: As Elena, I want to edit a finished workout, so that I can fix mistakes I notice later. The flow identifies its UI controller, domain service and data boundary.
Carries all original validation rules into finished-record correction and derived views.
sequence/FW-18.mmd: As Elena, I want to delete a finished workout after confirming, so that accidental or test entries do not distort my history and graphs. The flow identifies its UI controller, domain service and data boundary.
Explains both user-visible permanent deletion and internal synchronization tombstones.
sequence/FW-19.mmd: As Priya, I want to narrow my history to a date range or to one exercise, so that I can find a specific period or lift without scrolling. The flow identifies its UI controller, domain service and data boundary.
Prevents date and exercise filters from accidentally replacing each other.
sequence/FW-20.mmd: As Marcus, I want to see a graph of my total volume for one exercise over time, so that I can tell whether I am lifting more than before. The flow identifies its UI controller, domain service and data boundary.
Ties exercise chart points directly to converted source sets and workout IDs.
sequence/FW-21.mmd: As Marcus, I want to choose the period shown on a graph, so that I can compare recent weeks with the longer trend. The flow identifies its UI controller, domain service and data boundary.
Keeps chart, table and explanation synchronized when period controls change.
sequence/FW-22.mmd: As Priya, I want to see my total volume per week across all weight-based exercises, so that I can tell whether I am training more overall. The flow identifies its UI controller, domain service and data boundary.
Defines weekly bucketing, zero weeks and the zero-denominator comparison case.
sequence/FW-23.mmd: As Elena, I want to see my total reps per workout for a reps-only exercise, so that I can follow progress on bodyweight exercises. The flow identifies its UI controller, domain service and data boundary.
Avoids assigning weighted volume or kilograms to reps-only exercises.
sequence/FW-24.mmd: FW-24: Select a point, open workout

As Marcus, I want to select a point on a graph to see its date and value and open that workout, so that I can understand an unusually high or low session. The flow identifies its UI controller, domain service and data boundary.
Preserves the link from a chart/table point to the actual contributing records.
sequence/FW-25.mmd: As Elena, I want to save the exercises of a finished workout as a named template, so that I can start my usual routine again without re-entering it. The flow identifies its UI controller, domain service and data boundary.
Makes templates independent exercise lists rather than copies of performed sets.
sequence/FW-26.mmd: As Marcus, I want to start a workout from a template, so that its exercises are already in the workout when I begin. The flow identifies its UI controller, domain service and data boundary.
Defines archived exercise handling and avoids copying prescribed loads into a workout.
sequence/FW-27.mmd: FW-27: Create and edit a template

As Priya, I want to create and edit a template by choosing exercises myself, so that I can set up my plan at home before going to the gym. The flow identifies its UI controller, domain service and data boundary.
Captures name validation, ordering and independent template edits.
sequence/FW-28.mmd: As Marcus, I want to delete a template, so that I can retire routines I no longer use. The flow identifies its UI controller, domain service and data boundary.
Ensures deleting a saved routine never deletes workouts started from it.
sequence/FW-29.mmd: As Tomás, I want to make the text larger, so that I can read my workouts and summaries without straining. The flow identifies its UI controller, domain service and data boundary.
Makes large text a persistent app-wide presentation behavior.
sequence/FW-30.mmd: As Tomás, I want to see each weight with its equivalent in the other unit, so that I know how much to load when a gym’s plates use a different unit. The flow identifies its UI controller, domain service and data boundary.
Uses one conversion/formatting path for every equivalent weight display.
sequence/FW-31.mmd: FW-31: Enter a set in either unit
As Tomás, I want to enter a set in either kg or lb, so that I can log what the plates say without converting. The flow identifies its UI controller, domain service and data boundary.
Prevents a unit switch from silently reinterpreting a number without conversion.
